title: Kernel graffiti: morning quick-capture
content:
morning graffiti - quick capture (not polished)

Top-of-mind items to triage and experiment on today:

1) intermittent kv-cache poisoning on prod-dedicated-2
- symptoms: requests for long-prefix workloads sometimes fall back to cpu-path after 2-10s; observed TTL spike and cache miss storm.
- quick repro attempt: replay trace RW-20260311-1442 (from RW-2987). local dev repro with --seq-len=1024 + synthetic prefix hits 40% miss for key shards 3..5.
- hypothesis: race between async cache writeback and eviction thread when batch flush > threshold (16MB). eviction logic uses LRU but metadata updates not multi-thread safe under high append.
- immediate mitigation: lower async_batch_flush_ms to 20ms on dedicated-2 pool (canary) + throttle concurrent writes.
- TODO: add stricter atomic update path in cache metadata (Rajiv) — small patch to use per-shard mutexes (see PR #542). follow up perf cost.

2) micro-batching oddness on short-lived routes (chat-streaming)
- observed: batching window sometimes collapses to 1 when concurrent_senders spikes briefly even though target batch_size=8.
- notes: suspect poor window warmup with rapid open/close patterns (mobile clients).
- experiment plan: implement exponential backoff for window shrinkage instead of immediate collapse (Aisha to pair). write quick flag feature gate 'microbatch-soft-shrink'.
- measurement: add histogram for effective batch sizes over 24h and compare route /v1/chat-stream vs /v1/generate.

3) tail latency debugging checklist
- gather traces (x-ray) for top-5 tail traces last 2 hours: ids RW-TL-3409, RW-TL-3412, RW-TL-3417.
- check kernel preemption logs: kernel-sched* events around timestamps. look for CPU steal or GPU context switch thrash.
- check model-compile fallsbacks (quantized->fp16) that increase kernel launch time. add a label in traces if fallback occurred.

4) adhoc perf microbench notes
- run ./bench/micro_batch --model small-llama --batch 1..16 --seq 256 repeat 10, collect p50/p95/p99. attach csv to RW-2987.
- add a toggled path to disable 'prefetch_kv' and compare throughput — hypothesis: prefetch helps for long sequences but harms very short seq due to extra memcpy.

5) small triage items (one-liners)
- investigate noisy gc logs on worker-45 (likely python wrapper leak). quick grep: last restart 2026-03-11T03:12Z.
- add alert: 'kv-cache-miss-rate > 5% for 5m' to console (temp).
- clarify SLA fallback policy doc: which model variants are allowed to serve when dedicated exhausted? follow up with product console team.

6) experiments I want to try this week (note to self)
- adaptive batch sizing: dynamic target batch based on route latency SLO and current queue depth. simulate using loadgen.
- compact metadata encoding for kv-cache (8->6 bytes) to reduce memory churn. prototype in a branch and measure gc.
- try a tiny per-request path that avoids scheduler for ultra-low-latency routes (bypass pool) — measure cost of lost packing.

7) meeting talking points for 10:30 sync with SRE and infra
- rolling canary for async_batch_flush_ms change: plan, rollback, metrics to watch.
- potential impact on memory pressure if we reduce flush interval (more frequent smaller writes) — need to track wall-clock memory usage.
- request: allocate 2 extra p3 nodes for a controlled soak of microbatch-soft-shrink.

8) random thoughts / unresolved questions
- if we make cache metadata updates lock-free using CAS, will we still hit ABA with recycled entries? need safe epoch-based reclamation.
- would prefix-aware batching (grouping requests by shared first k tokens) improve hit rate significantly? how much overhead to compute signatures at ingress?

CLI commands I ran this morning (paste for reproducibility):
- ./scripts/trace-fetch rw-20260311-1442 --out traces/20260311-1442.json
- jq '.events[] | select(.type=="kv")' traces/20260311-1442.json | head -n 100
- docker exec -it runtime-worker-45 /bin/bash -c 'grep -i oom /var/log/runtime/*.log || true'

Next immediate actions (today):
- ping Rajiv about PR #542 and schedule 30m pair to review mutex approach (Elliot)
- flip microbatch-soft-shrink feature gate in staging and gather 2h histograms (Aisha)
- open small doc for 'cache-atomicity-proposal' and link to RW-2987 (Elliot)
- add transient alert to console for kv miss rate (SRE)

Notes to self: keep these scratchy, move actionable items to tickets asap. this file is my rapid capture; might prune and push to confluence later.

-- E.C.
